text:
ben: FYI rvx bring-up in staging shows odd behavior on code-like queries (function/identifier search). Overall NDCG@10 +0.8% but MRR@5 for identifier queries (contains `_` or `.`) down -5.7%. Short thread to triage.

faye: Oof. Paste the slices?

ben: quick table from eval-run-ccc:
```
metric       overall  id_queries (has . or _)  natural_queries
NDCG@10      +0.8%    +0.5%                   +1.0%
MRR@5        -0.4%    -5.7%                   +0.9%
Top1_rate    -0.9pp   -6.8pp                  +0.5pp
```
notes: rvx changed token pipeline to aggressive identifier_split + stopword_strip (removes "get"/"set"/"the"), and we deployed int8 PTQ with asymmetric rounding.

nate: Identifier splitting could break exact-id matching if underscores get split into subtokens or removed. stopword_strip removing "get" might change the preferred doc.

faye: Also check candidate_normalize: we enabled normalize_punctuation=collapse which can drop dots in `foo.bar`. That would definitely break exact-match anchors.

ben: Good point. Running quick ablation: toggle {identifier_split, normalize_punctuation, stopword_strip, quant}. Eval command: 
```
./eval_rerank.sh --model rvx --dataset code_holdout_v1 \
  --identifier_split {on,off} --norm_punct {collapse,keep} \
  --stopword_strip {on,off} --quant {fp16,int8}
```
queued.

eval-bot: Job 1221 queued by ben. ETA ~14m.

nate: Add exact_identifier_match and top1_confidence metrics. MRR move likely from top1 loss.

eval-bot: Job 1221 finished. Quick results:
- identifier_split=off, norm_punct=keep, stopword_strip=off, quant=fp16 -> id_queries MRR recovered +5.3% (near baseline)
- same but quant=int8 -> recovered +4.4% (int8 loses ~0.9pp)
- only turning off stopword_strip recovers +3.8%
- only keep norm_punct recovers +2.9%

faye: So main drivers: punctuation normalization and stopword stripping. identifier_split also matters but less so. quant is a small negative amplifier.

ben: Current top1_prob for id_queries was -6.8pp; with norm_punct=keep it improved +3pp, with stopword_strip=off +4.1pp. Combined they explain most of the delta.

nate: Actionable: revert normalize_punctuation for queries that look like code (regex: contains [._] or matches camelCase/underscore pattern), and disable stopword_strip for queries with fewer than 6 tokens or that match code regex. Low-risk rule.

faye: Agree. Also add a unit test in CI: a small harness that runs a tiny code-holdout and ensures any tokenizer/normalizer changes don't reduce exact_identifier_match by >1pp. Add to PR checklist.

ben: Filed rollout: https://go/rollout/rvx-code-query-exceptions (10% 2h -> 50% 2h -> 100%). Will patch tokenizer config first.

ci-bot: Created PR #7643 to add code-query regex exception and CI harness.

nate: One more follow-up: int8 still shows ~1pp penalty on identifier MRR even with formatting fixes. Might be PTQ bias on small vocab embeddings. We'll run a targeted calibration on embedding layers for code slice.

ben: Good call. For release plan we'll ship formatting fixes first then do a small calibration on int8 if A/B still shows leftover delta. Blocking Dedicated rollout until A/B confirms.

faye: Nice triage. Learned: seemingly innocuous normalizers (collapse punctuation, stopword strip) can wreck exact-match heavy slices like code search even if overall ranking metrics look fine.

ben: Will post A/B numbers in this thread after 2h. Thanks all. :rocket:
